speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with an episode of loss of consciousness; can you describe exactly what happened during the event and how long you were unconscious?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That loss of consciousness occurring immediately after urination is a classic sign of neurocardiogenic syncope triggered by the Valsalva maneuver; did you feel any warning symptoms like lightheadedness, nausea, or sweating right before you passed out?

REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
REQUEST IMAGES: None required at this stage.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vasovagal syncope secondary to micturition.

The timing of your fainting spell immediately after urination is a hallmark of neurocardiogenic syncope, and the rapid recovery without confusion or incontinence further supports this. An ECG has been ordered to rule out underlying cardiac arrhythmias, which is the standard of care before considering other causes.
